_comment: Round-10 fix wave (Phase 3). Inputs: ISSUES.json and JUDGE.json on handoff/audit-r10-register (PR #2244, head d23205d13); CATCHUP-JUDGE.json at 33ffa7aa9; issues #2219-#2243; the orchestrator's plan (owner-reported, study, instrument and arch groups).

One entry per pull request. Grouped by class first, then classes touching the same owning seam merged; a group that would span more than one owning module is split, so a class issue can sit in several groups. `fixes` names the issues a group closes because it is the deepest group holding them (wave depth); the body says Part of for the rest. Where two holders are unordered and the deeper one merges first, the orchestrator moves the closing keyword to the last merge and verifies the close.

Every group holds at least one filed issue. The 22 group issues from dev/audit/rounds/round10/ROSTER-ISSUES.json (#2252-#2273) and the four class issues N-leaf-imports-solver, N-restore-race, N-order-coupling and N-solve-recompute (#2247-#2250) are wired into `issues`; no pending token remains. The roster check: no group without an issue, and no open round-10 issue without a group.

`files` is the conflict map's input and `after` serialises every pair of groups sharing a file, except the shared test and record files every group appends to (tests/features.py, tests/entities.py, tests/seam_map.json, tests/finite_boundary.py, tests/guard_pins.py, tests/dst_checks.py, tests/arch_score_head.py, tests/structure_budgets.json, the mutation ledger): a conflict there is a rebase the fixer seat resolves at its own merge base, re-deriving every budget figure.
Hot files (const.py, coordinator.py, optimizer.py, config_flow.py, the card script) carry an architect note in each group's brief (orchestrator.md section 5, fixer.md step 17).

Ordering rules applied: high and critical first; structure-reducing groups before code-adding ones; defect fixes before the large arch moves on the same files; the deep-link helper before UX-SETUP, UX-HEALTH and ADVISOR; RATIO-SITES before SCORES, the identifiability groups and TRUST-RELATIVE; HEAT-METER before COP-GATE; ARCHSCORE-COVERAGE before the D7 M7/M8 policy fold (R10-BRIEFS-FOLD).

`wave` is the dependency depth (1 = startable now). `size` is S/M/L/XL by diff and seam count. `severity` is the judge's (catch-up judge where it re-rated); owner-reported, study and instrument groups carry no judge rating and are entered as medium unless the owner said otherwise.

Constraint: a new key added to INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/const.py needs its on-change decision in the same pull request. At 07b83e9b2 the module holds a second table, INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES, which is the limit for a source never seen re-reporting an unchanged value. A test modelling a dead meter must therefore re-report the unchanged value (last_reported past last_updated, which inputs.source_polls reads at 07b83e9b2) before it falls silent. On an unbounded key, a FakeState with only an old last_updated now reads fresh. Take the gate lease beyond `stress.py`: `tests/gate_lock.py` gains a **slot-counted lease beside the exclusive one** — default **4** slots (a slot-count environment override, clamped to ≤ 4 without the owner), taken FIFO with the existing lease/expiry/orphan-steal machinery, released on exit; `needs-lease` grows a third answer **`slot`** beside `lease`/`none`. `prepr.sh` takes **one slot for its whole life** and exports a slot-label environment variable so its heavy steps (self-test ~172 s, mutants drive ~127 s, the scoped closures recordings) run *inside* that slot and do not re-acquire; `tests/derive_closures.sh` takes a slot only **standalone** (else two seats' four-lane derives stack to eight). The exclusive lease stays exclusive for the scripts whose numbers are comparable only alone — `stress.py` and, within the mutation pool, `harness_headers.py`. The rule: **machine-measuring ⇒ exclusive; multi-minute CPU-bound ⇒ join the four slots; seconds ⇒ no lease** (`structure.py` ~11.5 s and `layout.py` ~17 s are the seconds side; the recordings ≥ 69 s are the minutes side). `gate-scoping.md` and `nudge.md` §8 state the scope and that the lease — not the tick's count — is the enforcement.

groups.architect_note: ARCHITECT NOTE (orchestrator, binding under fixer.md step 17). Owning seams: thermal_model.flow_setpoint_for_level with pump_arbiter._flow_target and _flow_inlet_c (mapping), and the objective's level rounding in optimizer.py with its start set (flat zone). Shape: a sliding setpoint scale anchored at measured tank temperature plus a minimum lift, not a better binary choice; the solver scores levels without a zero-slope region below the minimum. coordinator.py should not change (the arbiter has the tank temperature). Optional: count radiator water in the system heat capacity. Controls: flat-price run publishes the same plan; full power still writes the configured ceiling. Mutants to kill: mapping bottom reverted to return temperature; smoothing or new starts dropped (a buffered rounded install with price spread must book above minimum in the cheapest steps, flat unchanged).
groups.brief: On installs whose pump power is set through a heating-flow setpoint behind a buffer tank and mixing valve, the setpoint is a power command (owner, 2026-10-19: a 55 degree setpoint in short slots applies maximum power while the system volume rises slowly). Two defects keep the plan at the minimum level all day despite price spread. (1) flow_setpoint_for_level maps the minimum level to the return temperature (35 C without a return sensor), which on a 23-34 C tank yields about a third of the planned draw. (2) Rounding inside the objective makes cost flat between 0 and the minimum level, so the solver stalls there. Fix: anchor the power-to-setpoint mapping at the measured tank temperature plus a minimum lift, sliding to the configured ceiling at full power; remove the solver flat zone (smooth or duty-cycle scoring of rounded levels, or high-power starts in the cheapest steps). Flat-price null control mandatory: at flat prices the published plan is unchanged and every gain claim is net of the flat-price run. Do not wire draw_range.planned_range into the solve until the mapping is fixed. Owner requirement (2026-10-19): work across as many setup combinations as possible. The minimum-level anchor comes from whichever sensors are configured, in a documented precedence over heat-pump return, heat-pump outgoing flow, buffer tank and post-mixing-valve supply, falling back to the current no-sensor default. Heat-pump outgoing and return temperatures become optional config inputs, and leaving them unset keeps current behaviour exactly. Tests cover the sensor combinations as a matrix, with a mutant per precedence rung.

Carried from #2465 (R10-SETPOINT-BOOST) at afabd5b6; the ceiling probe owns these:
- **The mapping reads the water temperature only at the floor.** The floor is relative to the inlet, the ceiling is absolute, and the levels between are linear in configured power. A pump's draw follows the set-point minus the water temperature, and it saturates. So the same level commands a different power at every tank temperature, and the gain between set-point and draw is unidentified on a set-point-driven install. Identifying that gain is R10-CEILING-PROBE's: its cheap-night `sysid.py` experiment measures drawn power against the commanded set-point. The booked-vs-delivered heat that follows from the gap is R10-DEMAND-OVERBOOK's, carried under `## Forward-carry`.
- **Reaching the real maximum** needs either p_max configured at its true value (an owner question for tvofi, who is adjusting the config) or a deliberate ceiling probe. The probe is R10-CEILING-PROBE, folded into the cheap-night system-identification experiment (`sysid.py`). B is its prerequisite: the window now admits ceiling-commanded evidence only.
- **Idle draw can absorb compressor draw.** If the gate is not truly off (the compressor runs at the gate on a cold inlet), the learned idle median takes in compressor draw. The reviewer measured that at a gate-held draw of 1.4 kW, 24 of 72 running samples drop and the low end moves from 1.35 to 1.8 kW. `follows_ask` uses the same filter. Carried from #2469 (R10-UPDATE-PR-LOCK) at 931e9a0f, round-4 split under the three-round rule:
- A SIGKILLed run's holder frees the lock within 2 s while the push that run started may still be running in the worktree. Holding it until that push ends needs a drain of the run's process group, and in a container whose PID 1 reaps orphans late that drain's arm failed 7 of 7 runs (#2469 round 4).

(SIGINT does not reach it: bash starts the holder in the background, with SIGINT ignored.)
- Under `set -e`, any command inside `update_pr.sh` that exits 75 reads to the relay as BUSY and is retried rather than recorded. Today only the lock path exits 75.

What (e) asks for: an OPTIONAL thermal power entity, a config option beside the electrical power and flow entities. When it is configured, three consumers change -- (1) measured COP (thermal divided by electrical) feeds cop_scale learning directly, closing the weather-walking failure flow_lift.py documents, where cop_scale absorbs lift-driven COP drop as degradation on direct plants because compute_cop's flow-temperature term never applies; (2) the house-heat-loss learner takes measured delivered heat as its input instead of the commanded-power assumption or the room-residual fit; (3) the capacity envelope samples at all loads rather than only the >=95%-of-p_max steps it is restricted to today (coordinator.py, the envelope sampler added with the probe). Absent the entity, behaviour is exactly as it is now and the goldens are byte-identical; a fully metered install with the option unset must reproduce today's figures. Use the one install-capability probe (writes available, measured power present, frequency present) that (a), (c) and (d) already read rather than adding a second. The tree already derives thermal output from a flow meter and the supply/return temperatures (flow_meter.thermal_output_kw = flow x 4.186 x dT), but only when no measured power and no frequency signal exist; this option is the direct-sensor case, so say in the body how the two interact and which wins when both are configured.

groups.brief: Found by the 2026-10-20 slip screen of the last 500 merged pull requests, from #2393's own Forward-carry, which routed this to the dimension briefs in prose. No dimension brief ever gained the text and round 10 never reproduced it, so the defect is still in the tree. What #2393 recorded, verbatim: the heat-loss learner replays against ThermalState.room_temperature's 21.0 C default on installs with no indoor temperature entity, because _learning_frozen deliberately does not freeze an unconfigured slot (coordinator.py:6552-6559). The consequence: on such an install the learner fits house-heat-loss against a constant 21 C, so the coefficient it learns is quietly wrong, and a wrong heat-loss coefficient propagates into every plan built on it. What to build: a measured decision, not a guess -- either freeze the heat-loss learning on that install with a visible reason (the same shape (c) of #1955 used for the unmetered learner), or drive the replay from an observable that exists without an indoor sensor; choose between them by measuring which one stops the coefficient drifting on a replay of a real install, and say which in the body. Null control owed: an install WITH an indoor temperature entity must be byte-identical to today, golden fixtures included. Do not widen _learning_frozen for configured slots; the defect is the unconfigured case only.

Fold (e) of #1930, deferred as high risk and lost: #1975 closed #1930 with (a)-(d), the words survive only inside the done group R9-F10.16's brief, and nothing in round 10 names it (found by the 2026-10-20 slip screen). The option, verbatim: skipping a driver on a mutant line it never executes. In practice the mutation lane runs every driver against every mutant, and a driver whose tests never reach the mutated line cannot kill it, so those runs are pure cost; skipping them saves CI time with the same killing power. The risk is asymmetric: one wrong skip loses a real killer, the mutant survives, and the lane either reports a false survivor or hides a genuine test gap -- which is why the deferral demanded a 595-row replay. Build it measure-first, in this order, and do not reorder: (1) build the 595-row replay -- for every mutant/driver pair, record from a real run whether that driver executes the mutated line, and land the matrix as a checked-in artifact with its command; (2) enable a skip only where a matrix row says the driver never reaches the line -- no skip may be enabled without its row, and a pair with no row must run; (3) prove with a null control that the kill set under skipping is identical to the kill set without it on the whole matrix, and that the survivor set is unchanged. If the matrix shows no pair is skippable, record that measurement and stop: the answer is then a recorded refusal, not a feature. The 595 figure is the row count from #1930's harness at that head -- re-derive it, do not carry it.

No loop writes a liveness signal anyone outside the host can read: tick_loop.sh writes a local board, state_docs.py's beat pushes only when main moves, and wt_sync.sh only when a tree is dirty. Each tick pass updates one ref, heartbeat/orchestrator, to a commit whose message carries the pass time and the relay and tick return codes, pushed with the seat's existing credential. A watcher outside the host (an owner-scheduled cloud task) reads the ref's committer date and alerts the owner when it is older than 20 minutes. groups.brief: The merge pitch as a mechanism, not an agent's turn (Lean flow study, mechanisation). Today the orchestrator builds every train queue by hand: merge_train.py documents the queue schema in its docstring and nothing writes one, so a pitch happens only when an agent's turn assembles pull request numbers, verdict heads and comment ids. Add a queue builder to merge_train.py that writes the queue from the open non-record pull requests whose newest verdict is merge at the head or carries to it, oldest first, and leaves budget and policy paths to the serial route the batch admit already applies. Then run tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py, then train.sh with --bot-prs --approval-carry --pre-flight, once per pitch, from the tick loop, and never while a train's pidfile is live. Every merge goes through merge_pr.sh or the train, which approve (app_approve.sh, or tvofi's review under the mandate on a code-owned path) before merging; a posted merge verdict is not a GitHub approval. Controls: a fixture with one verdicted head, one carried head, one head the carry refuses, one blocked verdict and one budget file builds exactly the expected queue; an empty queue starts no train; a live pidfile starts none; mutants of each admission rule fail named arms. groups.brief: adopt one arm only, as new fly-in R10-FLY-ROW-HEAD-CARRY (S/M, lane F, code-owned .github/workflows/*: cite mandate approval 6319294694), with after-edges R10-CI-LAYOUT-P2 and R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC. The arm: carry the previous head's completed Tests, CodeQL, Hassfest and Validate results to a head whose diff from that head is exactly the PR's own dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md. Decline every path-filter skip and every policy, docs or fixture .md relaxation -- measured from one bulk Actions listing (5 calls of up to 1000 runs, 2026-10-21 00:00-21:00Z; 3 windows capped at 1000, so this is a sample) and git diffs between consecutive PR heads. "run-min" is a run's started-to-updated wall time, not billed job minutes. (1) Shares, over 116 consecutive PR-head pairs and 11066 PR run-min: 47 heads add only merges from main (3889 run-min), 10 carry code (1417), and 59 are .md-only (2399, 21.7%). All 59 .md-only heads are the record class: delivery rows only. Policy, docs and fixture .md heads number 0, so relaxing them buys nothing. For docs and fixtures the scoped gate already runs 0 scripts, and policy .md must always run policy_lint and the code-owner rule. (2) The record class comes in two shapes. (a) record/autofix PRs: 37 heads, 579 run-min (5.2%), whose Tests already run scoped (about 3.8 min a head). A job-level path skip of the code-only workflows would save about 290 run-min (2.6%), but it makes required contexts report a skipped success with no run behind it, which is a weaker guarantee than any run. Declined. (b) open_pr.sh's second push, the row-only head: 22 heads, 1820 run-min on the row heads (16.4%), plus 1277 on the code heads it superseded. Only 3 of 22 superseded heads finished Tests; the rest were cancelled by concurrency. The gap between the two heads has a median of about 8 min and a tail of 198 and 500 min (refused second pushes, P13's class). The PR's whole diff is code, so a path filter can skip nothing here. Only a carry keyed on the head-diff can avoid the re-run. The writer-side fix (one push) is impossible because the row's name needs the PR number. Moving the row out of the PR changes delivery-status-tracking.md (policy, moratorium 0012). (3) The carry. No cancel when the superseding head's diff is exactly delivery/<N>.md of this PR. The row head's Tests, CodeQL, Hassfest and Validate contexts post head1's completed conclusions under the same check names and app, so the ruleset is unchanged. Governance (record, delivery-status, policy-docs) and PR contract are never carried and always run. Estimated saving: about 49 run-min per opened PR (today about 3097 run-min for 22 opens; after the carry, about 2020), about 10% of PR CI, plus about 8 min of lead time per open (CI finishes at T, not gap+T). (4) Ordering. After R10-CI-LAYOUT-P2, because the same workflow files are under a design-approved consolidation into one umbrella required check, which leaves one context to mirror instead of four, and the P2 ruleset cut-over is the orchestrator's. After R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC, which removes the 198 and 500 min refused-second-push tail. No open PR overlaps beyond #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1, tests.yml, governance.yml). (5) Null control (fixtures in the fly-in's self-test, plus one live planted head on a throwaway PR): a row-only head-diff carries. Row plus a one-byte CLAUDE.md edit does not carry, and policy-docs (policy_lint) goes red. Row plus a new unclassified .md does not carry, and Tests' entities goes red ("these force the FULL suite when touched"). A row for another PR's number, or a body the contract refuses, does not carry, and PR contract and delivery-status go red. A carried head whose head1 failed carries the failure, never a success. Brief addition: "carry, never skip: a head is row-only iff `git diff <prev-head> <head> --name-only` is exactly dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md of this PR and prev-head is its first parent; on such a head, concurrency keeps prev-head's runs and the carry posts their completed conclusions under the same context names; Governance and PR contract always run; each arm of the null control above is a named fixture and a file-scoped mutant".

Triage P-B (s4, batch 3, 2026-10-22, accepted), verbatim:
## P-B tick_loop.sh runs stale code: freshness check

VERDICT: ACCEPT -> R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF (not-started, S, files include tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh and cloud_relay.sh),
plus a forward-carry to R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's design (finding-propagation) because the same hazard moves to beatd.py.

Measured facts (origin/main tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh):
- It does no self-check at all. No `git` call, no SHA, no version in the banner or the heartbeat message. Each pass runs
  `$HERE/cloud_relay.sh pass` and `$HERE/orchestrator_tick.py` from whatever checkout it started in; only `tick_loop.sh` itself is
  read once. So a checkout never updates and every fix to those files is invisible to a running loop.
- The stale checkout 16a8240f1 (2026-10-22 08:11 +0200) is 506 commits behind origin/main fef4a1351; 119 touch tools/audit/seat and
  28 touch cloud_relay.sh, tick_loop.sh or orchestrator_tick.py. The hold check landed in cfa89d24f (R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD).
  A path filter on tools/audit/seat therefore cuts the restart rate from 506 to 119 candidates.
- Ownership: no group owns it. R10-RCA-ORCH-CONTINUITY and R10-FLOW-ANDON (tick_loop.sh, both done) cover liveness (heartbeat), not
  code freshness, so the heartbeat reads healthy while the code is old. R10-ORCH-MACHINERY (L, not-started) moves the relay to a
  launchd-supervised beat; its brief has no clause on which checkout the beat runs, so the hazard would carry over. FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF
  and R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN are the not-started groups on tick_loop.sh; REVIEW-FF is S and sits on the relay_start lines.
Design (narrower than the proposal):
- Do not fast-forward by default. The loop is documented as a read-only driver, and orch-wt is a worktree other seats may share
  (a dirty tree or a detached HEAD would make `merge --ff-only` fail or surprise).
- Each pass: `git -C $HERE fetch -q origin main` (a git fetch, no API) and count `HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat`. Put
  `code=<sha7> behind=<N>` in the TICK-PASS banner and the heartbeat message, so staleness shows off-host.
- If behind>0 and the tree is clean and `merge --ff-only` succeeds: `bash -n` the new tick_loop.sh, then `exec bash "$0" "$@"`. Otherwise
  print `TICK-STALE behind=N` and carry on (never exit: a stopped loop is worse than a stale one).
Null control: a throwaway origin whose main did not move prints behind=0 and does not exec. Mutant: drop the path filter or the
`bash -n` guard. Cost: S; one fetch per 300 s pass, 288 a day, no API.
Binding constraints: tick_loop.sh is measured by the mutant file (new arm takes a per-file id, e.g. tick_loop-N); a new git call
sites need no PUSHERS entry (fetch only). The exec guard matters: a broken main would crash-loop the driver, so the `bash -n`
check and the single re-exec per pass are part of the carry.

Detect that the checkout is behind origin/main and restart between passes; never fast-forward in place under a running relay.

Measured facts: #2626's head moved 4 times because a 30 h loop ran a stale cloud_relay.sh; this is the second instance of the class (P4, 2026-10-21, was closed as "restart after a merge that touches tick_loop.sh or cloud_relay.sh"), and the recurrence that decision named. A fast-forward of the checkout each pass is unsound at origin/main tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh: the loop is a bash script read incrementally and it detaches cloud_relay.sh (RELAY_HOLDER, header lines 1-22), so rewriting either file while it runs corrupts the pass or a relay in flight, and a dirty or branch-checked-out tree makes the ff fail or move a branch. R10-ORCH-MACHINERY, the earlier candidate, is absorbed and is not valid.
Mechanism: each pass, `git fetch -q origin main` (git, not API), count `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat tools/pr tools/audit/carry_audit.py` (only the paths the loop runs); above 0 print a `TICK-STALE <utc> behind=<n>` banner on the pass line; above a bound N (default 25 commits, or any change to tick_loop.sh or cloud_relay.sh themselves) and with no relay in flight (the flock is free) and a clean detached tree, `git checkout -q --detach origin/main` and exec the new tick_loop.sh with the same args; otherwise refuse the pass with rc and the banner. The restart point is between passes, never mid-relay.
Alternatives rejected: R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN (M), R10-ORCH-BEATD (L; its supervised beat may replace the loop, so the check moves with the loop and BEATD's brief should say so). This group already edits relay_start in tick_loop.sh (P15), so the check lands in the same file without a second PR.

findings: nightly-status NIGHTLY ABSENT misdiagnoses a workflow younger than its first cron slot
groups.brief: nightly-status (tests/nightly_status.py, classify(), the ABSENT arm around l.346) turns every PR head and main red with 'NIGHTLY ABSENT: no scheduled run of the workflow was found at all ... GitHub disables schedules on repositories with no recent activity'. Measured 2026-10-22: nightly.yml (cron '17 2 * * *') reached main with #2585 (fae523a14, 08:05Z), after that day's 02:17Z slot; `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/workflows/nightly.yml` gives state=active, created 2026-10-22T08:05:56Z; `actions/workflows/nightly.yml/runs?event=schedule` total_count 0. So the schedule is NOT disabled: the workflow is younger than its first slot, and the message's stated cause is false. Every PR must answer the red in its body until the first scheduled run (pr-contract refused #2622 for it). Fix: distinguish (a) no cron slot has elapsed since the workflow reached main (read the workflow's created_at, or the first-parent commit that added the file, against the cron) -> a NEW/PENDING state that is not red, bounded to the first slot plus a grace (the cron period plus one hour), after which ABSENT reds as today; (b) the workflow's state is disabled_* -> ABSENT with GitHub's own reason (one read of actions/workflows/<file>); (c) active and past its first slot with no run -> ABSENT, worded without the inactivity claim. Keep classify() pure: new inputs are data, drivable from tests/entities.py. Controls: a fixture workflow created after the last slot reads NEW, not red; the same fixture 26 h later with no run reads ABSENT (null control: the grace does not hide a dead schedule); GitHub's disabled-for-inactivity workflow state reads ABSENT with that reason. Mutants: drop the grace bound -> the 26 h fixture passes wrongly; drop the state read -> the disabled fixture loses its reason. Spare the API: at most one extra read per run. If the first scheduled Nightly (due ~2026-10-23T02:17Z) lands before this merges, the fix still stands for the next new scheduled workflow (CI-LAYOUT P2b adds more).

carry: Lean flow study alignment (STUDY K17), binding on the build. The flow groups add work the approved design's beat and ledger must own, and they land first, so build them in: (0) The beat and every job it runs are detached processes, never an agent loop: in the live run of 2026-10-21, agent-based relay and tick loops ended their turns twice and had to be re-armed. beatd.py runs under daemonize.py and an operating-system supervisor that restarts it (launchd on the orchestrator's Mac, a user systemd unit elsewhere); an agent only reads beatd status and the journal, and never hosts a job. Jobs run concurrently: one job's run never delays another job's schedule, so a long handoff update (9 min observed on 2026-10-21) never leaves the tick board stale; the tick reads independently of the relay, as R10-TICK-RELAY-DECOUPLE (#2549) already does for tick_loop.sh. The handoff job honours R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD's hold file. (1) beatd.jobs.json gains two jobs: heartbeat (R10-FLOW-ANDON's job script; interval 300 s, timeout 60 s; its ref message carries beatd status, so a timed-out job alerts the owner, not only a dead host) and pitch (R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN's job script; on the hour or when the previous train ends; it only launches a detached train and reads the train-stop obligation, never waits on CI). (2) The ledger gains one event kind, postmerge-owed (producer: R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE's after-merge step; closer: that step's later success or an orchestrator disposition), because the design refuses an OWED shape with no ledger kind. (3) The handoff job carries R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY's body-only path unchanged and writes a disposition for the handoff-body ref it applies; it also does not move any pull request head while that pull request has a live reviewer in workers.json, which generalises R10-FLOW-ROSTER-FREEZE's predicate from the roster pull request to every head (fixer.md's freeze, made mechanical). (4) The seats job reads the dispatch records R10-FLOW-DISPATCH writes through bus.sh dispatch, which also gives the folded dispatch reason the round-3 review's N11-R found has no backing state. (4b) The ledger's verdict-unposted obligation closes only on a read-back: the posted pull request comment fetched and its first line matching the verdict and head, as comment-readback.md requires; a relayed claim that a verdict was posted is not a close (revision 8, observed live). (5) Is-main-red has one owner, the classifier #2570 and R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE share; the tick and the sweep do not grow a third. (6) The plan page: if R10-PLAN-ARTIFACT (#2558) merges first, part (3) extracts plan_model() from its code rather than building a second page, keeps the UNAVAILABLE page and the five mutation fixtures, and renders R10-FLOW-BOARD's flow section from the same model. (7) Inventory row M43 is stale: pr_cap.py gates dispatch, not opening, since #2525. Owner rulings (2026-10-21): the amendments are approved in this brief and the fix reviewer checks them against STUDY K17 at build (R12); the stranded-handoff aging defaults are 4 h to a DISPATCH line and 12 h to an owner flag (R14), built behind the switch the brief already asks for.

Count distinct (seam, attribute) pairs reached, including through a callee, or refuse a callee whose only body is a tuple of state reads. A failing test first: plant the alias and the getter on a clean tree; neither may move the figure, and that plant is also the null control. Use the finder's harness, the plants plant_p2.diff and plant_p3.diff in the ev/ directory of probe/rev-2620-654004be. Any budget re-record the metric change forces goes in the commit message, per CLAUDE.md rule 2, and a raise needs the owner's confirmation before the branch is pushed. Follow dev/governance/roles/fixer.md.

From #2662 round 2 (P2b coordinator, 2026-10-23): two holes let commit 767a06f7f (Co-Authored-By plus Claude-Session, authored 03:51Z on 2026-10-23, after the guard a4b27986 reached main at 7deeef1b6 06:08Z) reach a PR head. (1) Cloud and handoff pushes run no message guard: the cloud harness's own git push of handoff/<topic> and handoff_push.sh call no ref_privacy/attribution check. The u4 session's base 4200ea4c4 lacked both the guard and the .claude/settings.json attribution off-switch. (2) A commit first published through a ci-probe/* ref (ci_probe.py judges only the ref name and log lines, line ~180) is then exempt from app_push.sh's first-publish scope (line ~481), so cc51e6626 rode into #2662 unjudged. Fix both: judge commit messages on every push path that publishes commits, and make app_push judge every commit the PR adds over main, not only first-published ones. Each needs a failing fixture first and a null control. Open question for this group's design: 19 commits in P2b are AUTHORED 'Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>' (the cloud seat default identity). The owner's rule names footers, trailers and session links, not authors, so decide and record whether author identity is in scope; do not widen it silently.

groups.brief: Barrier for audit class I2 (RCA R10-RCA-INERT-CLOSURE-RECORDING, root-cause seat beside #2662, 2026-10-23). A closures recording carries an inert_reads split decided by the recording tree's INERT list; a later INERT_EXCEPT edit voids it, but merge and check trusted the split, so check passed vacuously and #2662's probe d5b053e went UNDER-SCOPED (32 min red FULL closures). Countermeasure built by the RCA seat: closure.py _load_recording re-splits each recording under the loading tree's INERT list for merge and check; ci_predict.py left_inert predicts UNDER-SCOPED statically when a diff edits tests/closure.py and a committed inert_reads file has left INERT while its script's closure omits it (prepr 6d, body_push). The countermeasure is built at handoff commit e9d169b7 (handoff/r10-rca-inert-closure-recording).
